Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation has a cost of $|V|-1$ because a vertex can have at most one outgoing edge to every other vertex in the graph. The average amortized cost is calculated by dividing the total sum of all operations by the number of vertices, which results in $\frac{|E|}{|V|}$.

* The maximum degree of any vertex in a simple directed graph with $|V|$ vertices is bounded by $|V|-1$, establishing the upper limit for the worst-case single operation.
* Aggregate analysis sums the costs of all $|V|$ operations to get $|E|$, and since there are $|V|$ operations, the amortized cost per operation is the ratio of total edges to total vertices.
